title: Inventory every count-claim guard that actually binds at HEAD, as a rerunnable tool
acceptance: An executable at tools/guard-inventory.mjs re-derives, from the repo at run time (never from hardcoded literals), a table of every guard in test/ whose subject is a numeric or structural COUNT claim about a document: for each one it names the file, the test title, the document claim it reads, where the expected value comes from (derived from src/corpus.js at test time vs. a literal written into the test file), and whether any guard asserts a floor on the SIZE of the suite itself. It also emits the current test-file line count per file and the total. The output must explicitly record the verdict on the inherited '>= 121 tests' floor premise: present or absent, with the evidence that settles it.
notes: PLAN confirmed by reading that NO literal suite-size floor exists in test/ — '121' occurs only in two prose comments in readme-matrix-consistency.test.js, and .github/workflows/test.yml carries an explicit written refusal to add a count assertion. So S-1's 'retire the COUNT floor' half likely has nothing to retire and W-2 is net-NEW tooling, not a replacement. The tool must SAY that rather than manufacture a floor to retire. Measured start: 129 tests across 7 files (readme-tags 31, args 28, cli 29, select 18, pipe 16, readme-matrix-consistency 5, node-support-citation 2); test/ 4,587 lines; src+bin 594. tools/ is outside the cited pathspec so creating it cannot falsify the README citation.

title: Build the detection floor: bounded, rule-generated mutation matrix with an identity control, baselined at 20b7ede
acceptance: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs exists, is zero-dependency, is NOT collected by the suite's own file glob, and adds zero tests. It states its generation rule in the file itself and enumerates at most 30 mutations produced by that rule — exactly one falsifying mutation per machine-checked document claim the W-1 inventory found — plus exactly ONE identity (no-op) mutation as converse control. For each mutation it applies the edit to a scratch copy, runs the suite there, records which NAMED guards fired, and leaves the working tree byte-identical. The identity control must leave the suite green; a mutation no guard catches is reported as SILENT, never omitted. Any claim the generation rule produces but the harness skips is listed with its reason. The baseline result against 20b7ede is recorded in tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json in a machine-comparable shape.
notes: Risk: ~30 suite runs. The suite spawns the real binary (cli/pipe tests) and shells out to git (node-support-citation), so the scratch copy must be a real git work tree or those two guards skip/fail for ENVIRONMENTAL reasons rather than because of the mutation — which would corrupt the matrix. Decide and STATE how the scratch copy handles git (clone vs worktree vs accept skips and mark N/A). Baseline at 20b7ede per S-1; HEAD 912a2a4 changed only .swarm/, so src/bin/test should be identical — confirm, do not assume.

title: Quote README's citation-selection rule verbatim in the history doc; check it from tools/, not a new test
acceptance: docs/node-support-citation-history.md contains README.md's citation-selection-rule sentence as an EXACT substring, attributed to README's '### Node support' section, in place of the current restatement; any surviving description of a superseded rule is clearly marked as history. The doc shows the derivation of applying the QUOTED rule to this tree and lands on the citation the README actually carries. A machine check of at most 30 added lines lives at tools/citation-rule-check.mjs (NOT a new test file), asserts file-to-file substring equality, is demonstrated failable (red when the quote is perturbed) and attributable (its failure names which document diverged), and is paired with a converse control showing it passes on the honest text.
notes: Divergence verified in SHAPE: README says the reference matrix is 'the matrix run for the push that carried the last change to src/, bin/, test/, or the workflow itself'; the history file's Q-8 entry states it as 'the most recent run whose cited commit's ... content is byte-identical to this tree's, without requiring that the cited commit be the one that produced the change.' Those select differently once later pushes exist that did not touch the pathspec. NOT executed against the Actions API — re-derive before acting. CONVENTION CONSTRAINT: the file's header promises the five blockquoted cycle entries are byte-identical to text removed from the README and must NOT be edited; the Q-7 and Q-8 entries are not blockquotes and ARE the editable surface. Putting the check in tools/ rather than test/ is deliberate: a sixth README guard test file is the run's explicit anti-goal, and docs/ + tools/ are outside the cited pathspec so this cannot open a citation window.

title: Count the citation two-commit tax over repo history, as a rerunnable tool that changes nothing
acceptance: tools/citation-tax.mjs walks committed history and derives, without hardcoding the answer: (a) how many commits touched the cited pathspec src/ bin/ test/ .github; (b) of those, how many landed while the citation guard existed and therefore made the README's cited diff non-empty at that commit — knowingly committed RED; (c) how many separate follow-up commits were spent re-citing; (d) the commit gap between each breakage and its repair, so same-commit and later-cycle repairs are distinguishable. It prints the exact derivation per event (breaking SHA, repairing SHA, gap) and ends with a plain recommendation on whether the ritual is intrinsic to a self-falsifying claim or an artifact of an over-claiming pathspec. It changes no pathspec, no assertion, no citation.
notes: PLAN's starting measurements, to be RE-DERIVED not trusted: 48 of 255 commits touch the pathspec across all history, but the guard only came into existence at 5f833ab, so 'every commit in history' is the wrong denominator and would inflate the tax. Honest denominator looks like the 6 pathspec-touching commits from 5f833ab forward (5f833ab, c08562b, c9dd7ff, 2b003ea, 4b63e91, 22fdeac→a302f71→7e50d6f), each of which appears to have cost a re-citation commit — i.e. ~100%. The guard also CHANGED SHAPE mid-history (c08562b made it fail loud on ambiguity; 2b003ea added the working-tree comparison), so 'would have turned red' is only well-defined against the guard version live at that commit — decide and state the convention.

title: Adjudicate the README Node-support matrix's 127-vs-129 numbers by measurement, as a rerunnable tool
acceptance: tools/matrix-adjudication.mjs re-derives, offline and from this checkout: (a) the four matrix rows as README states them; (b) how many tests the suite actually contains at HEAD and how many are the citation guard's two environment-conditional cases; (c) whether the cited base commit's src/bin/test/.github content is identical to this tree's, i.e. whether the citation rule still selects the cited run; (d) an explicit verdict — CORRECT-AS-CITED / STALE / UNDECIDABLE-OFFLINE — with the arithmetic that separates a stale current-state claim from a correctly-cited past-CI claim. If and ONLY IF the verdict is STALE is anything in README.md repaired.
notes: PREMISE CHECK from PLAN, recorded rather than planned around: S-5's framing is probably WRONG. The README rows report a REMOTE CI run, and CI checks out at depth 1, so the two node-support-citation tests SKIP there: 129/127/0/2. A local full clone runs those same two and they pass: 129/129/0/0. Both numbers are true of different environments; README's own standing limit 1 says exactly this, and readme-matrix-consistency.test.js's header already spells out why a local run cannot honestly be compared to the table. Most likely honest outcome is CORRECT-AS-CITED with a published explanation and ZERO README edits — which S-5 explicitly calls a PASS. The tool must be ABLE to reach STALE, but must not go looking for a repair. Offline anchor: archived CI evidence under .swarm/runs/ (cycle-005-verify-Q-8.txt names run 32405521233). Network/gh availability unverified — the tool must work without them.

title: Standing invariant: no corpus/--help byte movement, no dependency, no feature, green every commit bar one predicted window
acceptance: At every commit this run makes: src/corpus.js hashes to sha256 77a4de5c777a3bdb7099ea900e090831f3ec2d203e2346f9b9ac6419e545d09e; --help output hashes to sha256 d759d781ddcac780ed7eb13d7768e90f1bd52d707377fab50ff5c8f648dd5e64; the dependency surface is unchanged and nothing under tools/ imports outside node: builtins; no file under src/ or bin/ changes at all; and the suite is green at every commit EXCEPT a single citation window named as such, IN ADVANCE, in the commit message of the commit that opens it.
notes: An invariant, not a unit of work — conductor-held, never dispatched to a builder. Both hashes re-verified against HEAD 912a2a4 by PLAN and they match SPEC exactly, so the baseline is real, not inherited. W-7 is the ONLY item that can open a citation window (only item touching test/); every other item lands in tools/, docs/, or REPORT.md, all outside the cited pathspec. package.json must not be touched and appears in no files_hint.

title: Close KI-R6-3: consolidate the two guards reading the same 'Tags on exactly one entry' row, or publish the mutation that separates them
acceptance: The mutation falsifying README's 'Tags on exactly one entry' counts-table row is run through the detection floor and the set of NAMED guards it fires is recorded. If the two guards' firing sets are identical, exactly ONE is removed, and re-running the matrix shows every mutation detected at the 20b7ede baseline is still detected and the identity control still green. If the firing sets DIFFER, both are kept and the distinguishing mutation — the specific edit one catches and the other does not — is recorded in the test file naming what each guard uniquely catches. Either outcome closes it; 'keep both because removing one feels risky' does not. A drop in test count is a PASS.
notes: The two guards are in test/readme-tags.test.js: the test at ~line 434 (Q-4's structural replacement) and the second assertion inside the test at ~line 1598. The file's own comment block at lines 150-162 already concedes they are redundant in the strict sense — 'a wrong value in that row fails both and no mutation fails only one of them' — so consolidation is the likely branch. NOTE removing the ~1598 assertion would also drop the 'Tags on 2 or more entries' check, so target ~434 or be surgical. BIGGEST RISK IN THE PLAN: this is the ONLY item touching test/, inside the cited pathspec, so the commit that lands it makes the README's cited diff non-empty and turns both citation guards RED on a full clone. Closing the window needs a NEW Actions run id, which needs a successful push AND Actions API access — unverified from this environment (origin is https and master is level with origin/master, encouraging but not proof). Sequence LAST among code-touching items, GATE on a confirmed ability to obtain a run id, and predict the window in the commit message per S-8. There is no test/-free path to the removal branch.

title: Re-run the detection floor at final HEAD and prove no baseline detection was lost
acceptance: The mutation matrix is re-run against final HEAD and recorded in tools/mutation-matrix-final.json in the same machine-comparable shape as the baseline. A direct comparison shows no mutation detected at baseline 20b7ede is undetected at final HEAD, and the identity control is green in both. Any mutation whose FIRING GUARD changed (still detected, by a different named guard) is listed explicitly rather than folded into the pass. If any detection was lost, that is stated as a FAILURE with the specific mutation named — never rounded to a pass.
notes: This is what makes W-7's test-count DROP defensible rather than merely permitted. Must run AFTER W-7 lands or it measures the wrong tree. If W-7 ends in the 'keep both' branch this still runs and should show an identical matrix — a null result worth publishing as one. Depends on W-2's scratch-copy git strategy; if the two citation guards are N/A in the matrix they are N/A in BOTH runs and that must be stated rather than silently equal.

title: One entry point that re-runs every published finding, so S-6 is checkable rather than asserted
acceptance: tools/run-all.mjs invokes every measurement executable this run shipped, in a stated order, prints each one's re-derived output under a labelled heading, and ends with a one-line roll-up of which ran clean and which reported a problem. Zero-dependency, imports nothing outside node: builtins, not collected by the suite, leaves the tree byte-identical. Running it must be sufficient for a skeptical reader to re-derive every number this run publishes WITHOUT reading REPORT.md.
notes: Scope discipline: a dispatcher, not a report generator — it must not restate or interpret any finding, only re-run the tools that produce them. If the mutation matrix is slow (~30 suite runs), give it an opt-out flag and state in the file what the default excludes. This item is the concrete answer to the taste gate's catch that S-1/S-4/S-5 could all be discharged as prose.

title: REPORT.md: the measured before/after test/ line count and the S-7 escalation written as launchable brief text
acceptance: REPORT.md states the MEASURED before/after line count of test/ against the 4,587-line baseline, with the delta and which item produced it, and for every published finding names the executable under tools/ that re-derives it (no finding appears only as prose). It carries a single paragraph escalating the three user-visible changes locked out by the trickle brief for the fourth consecutive run — corpus depth, no-repeat rotation within a session, --tag discoverability — written as concrete brief text run #9 could be launched with VERBATIM: it must read as an instruction to a builder, not as a complaint, and a reader must be able to copy it into a kickoff without editing. Stated once, never re-derived elsewhere. Any must-have not verified appears as NOT-RUN with what would settle it, never as passed.
notes: The three escalated changes map to blocked items TS-1 (50 canon-only entries repeat by ~the 9th draw), TS-3 (Dijkstra 7 + Perlis 5 + Pike 5 = 17/50 = 34% of the corpus in three voices), TS-2/TS-6 (--tag vocabulary undiscoverable without jq; a retired tag name and a never-existing one are byte-identical in exit code, stdout and stderr) — measurements already on the record in backlog.json, to be CITED not re-derived (L-045). Honest expectation to carry in: if W-1 confirms no suite-size floor ever existed and W-5 lands CORRECT-AS-CITED, this run's only actual test/ REDUCTION is W-7's single removed guard, and test/ may end LARGER than 4,587 if any check is added — the before/after number is the run's own scoreboard and must be reported even when unflattering.
